output.headline: Approves minutes of the March 4, 2020 special Board meeting
output.summary: The Board is ratifying the minutes of its Special Meeting of March 4, 2020, which staff prepared shortly after the meeting. No dollar amount is involved.

output.headline: Awards Rook Electric $125,000 to maintain video surveillance systems at 30 sites
output.summary: The Board is approving a competitively bid agreement with Rook Electric of Oakland to maintain video surveillance systems, including servers, software, cameras and cabling, at 30 sites. Rook Electric was the lowest responsive and responsible bidder. Work is scheduled from September 24, 2020 to July 9, 2021.

output.headline: Pays a Piedmont consultant up to $25,920 to support teachers on drug and health education
output.summary: The Board is ratifying a contract with a Piedmont, CA consultant for 648 hours of support to teachers in online and in-person classrooms. The activities cover drug education, holistic health practices, and how race, law and politics affect incarceration and exploitation of youth. They also include Tobacco-Use Prevention Education (TUPE) services. The term is September 1, 2020 to June 30, 2021, which began before this vote.

output.headline: Pays an arts consultant up to $45,000 to help build the district's Strategic Arts Blueprint
output.summary: The Board is ratifying a contract with an Alameda, CA consultant who will work with the district's Visual and Performing Arts team. The goal is to plan and put in place support structures, called the Strategic Arts Blueprint, so district schools can use the arts to advance learning. The term is August 3, 2020 to June 30, 2021, which began before this vote.

output.headline: Buys MCT Technology's Carecloud software for early childhood programs, up to $14,037
output.summary: The Board is ratifying a contract with MCT Technology, Inc. of Diamond Bar, CA for its Carecloud software in the district's early childhood program. The software handles enrollment, eligibility, emergency contacts, electronic and contactless attendance, meal counts, licensing compliance and billing. The term is August 17, 2020 to June 30, 2021, which began before this vote.

output.headline: Adds $215,050 for Ninyo & Moore's soil sampling and environmental work at the Fremont construction project
output.summary: The Board is amending an environmental consulting agreement with Ninyo & Moore for added work at the Fremont New Construction Project. The work includes a Supplemental Sampling Technical Memo and more soil sampling at Increments 3 and 4, as directed by the state Department of Toxic Substances Control. The added $215,050 includes a $19,550 contingency, raising the maximum from $396,517 to $611,567 and extending the end date from December 31, 2020 to August 17, 2021.

output.headline: Adds $28,189 for Ninyo & Moore's operations and maintenance consulting at LaEscuelita Educational Center
output.summary: The Board is amending an engineering services agreement with Ninyo & Moore for extra operations and maintenance consulting at the LaEscuelita Educational Center project. This covers completed out-of-scope tasks and more tasks planned for 2020. The agreement's maximum rises from $48,340 to $76,529, and the end date moves from December 31, 2020 to June 30, 2021.

output.headline: Adds $11,857.10 for Nor-Cal Moving Services to relocate rooms at Glenview construction project
output.summary: This amendment pays Nor-Cal Moving Services of Hayward for extra moving work: relocating two rooms and items from the gym into classrooms for the Glenview New Construction Project. It raises the contract limit from $27,000.00 to $38,857.10. All other terms of the agreement stay the same, and the cost comes from the Measure J construction bond fund.

output.headline: Pays Tulum Innovative Engineering $98,000 to install phone and data cabling at Santa Fe special ed site
output.summary: The district hired Tulum Innovative Engineering of Oakland, the selected bidder in a competitive bid, to install about 300 network cables with patch panels, wire managers and jacks for the Santa Fe SPED @ Santa Fe project. The work covers about 85 phone lines, 143 computer lines and 4 fax lines. Work is scheduled to run from September 24, 2020 to December 23, 2020.

output.headline: Adds $6,000 for Nor-Cal Moving Services to move classroom furniture in Cole Administration relocation
output.summary: This amendment pays Nor-Cal Moving Services of Hayward for extra moving work: relocating all furniture from the classrooms into the multipurpose room for the Cole Administration Move Relocation Project. It raises the contract limit from $27,800.00 to $33,800.00. All other terms of the agreement stay the same, and the cost comes from the Measure J construction bond fund.

output.headline: Hires Project Support Services for $42,000 to help close out state approvals on construction projects
output.summary: The Board is approving a general services agreement with Project Support Services of Orange, CA. The firm will help the district finish and certify construction projects with the Division of the State Architect (DSA), the state office that sets school construction standards, on current and new projects. The agenda title says the contract was not competitively bid. Work runs from September 24, 2020 to June 30, 2021.

output.headline: Approves Bertrand, Fox, Elliott, Osman & Wenzel for general legal services, up to $95,200 a year
output.summary: The Board is ratifying a memorandum of understanding and engagement policy with Bertrand, Fox, Elliott, Osman & Wenzel Law Firm, with offices in Oakland and San Francisco, CA, to give the district legal services and general legal advice as needed. Spending is capped at $95,200 per fiscal year. The term is July 1, 2020 to June 30, 2022, which began before this vote.

The interns serve a group of ten elementary schools, with two interns at each site. The term is August 10, 2020 to June 30, 2021, which began before this vote.

output.headline: Pays We Lead Ours up to $90,000 to support teachers on drug and health education
output.summary: The Board is ratifying a contract with We Lead Ours of Oakland, CA for 2,250 hours of support to teachers in online and in-person classrooms. The activities cover drug education, holistic health practices, and how race, law and politics affect incarceration and exploitation of youth. They also include Tobacco-Use Prevention Education (TUPE) services. The term is September 1, 2020 to June 30, 2021, which began before this vote.

output.headline: Pays a clinical supervisor up to $25,000 for the newcomer student wellness team's social workers
output.summary: The Board is ratifying a contract with an Oakland, CA clinician to provide ongoing clinical supervision, in groups and one-on-one, for up to 8 unlicensed social workers and Marriage and Family Therapists (MFTs). They serve on the district's Student Newcomer Wellness Team. The term is August 15, 2020 to May 28, 2021, which began before this vote.

The term is July 1, 2020 to June 30, 2021, under Resolution No. 2021-0008. The agenda text does not state a dollar amount.

output.headline: Pays East Bay Agency for Children up to $25,000 for student therapy at Rudsdale Newcomer High School
output.summary: The Board is ratifying a contract with East Bay Agency for Children to offer therapeutic and case management services to students at Rudsdale Newcomer High School who are on Medi-Cal or moving onto it. The term is August 3, 2020 to June 30, 2021, which began before this vote.

output.headline: Pays Bay Area Community Resources up to $60,000 for the Young Hawks newcomer student program
output.summary: The Board is approving a contract with Bay Area Community Resources of San Rafael, CA to support newcomer students in the Young Hawks Program. Services include targeted academic support, family engagement, summer school for English Learners, violence prevention and gang intervention, drug abuse and mental health counseling, and court advocacy. The term is August 31, 2020 to May 28, 2021.

output.headline: Pays a consultant up to $30,000 to facilitate Strong Workforce career technical education projects
output.sourceIssueCandidate: The agenda title says the agreement is for 2020-2020, but the action text describes a 2020-2021 agreement running July 1, 2020 to June 30, 2021.
output.summary: The Board is ratifying a contract with an Oakland, CA consultant to provide professional facilitation of Strong Workforce and related Career Technical Education projects, as described in the contract's Exhibit A. The term is July 1, 2020 to June 30, 2021, which began before this vote.

The term is August 3, 2020 to June 30, 2021, which began before this vote.

output.headline: Revises five job descriptions and creates a new Accounts Payable Technician III job description
output.summary: The Board is adopting Resolution No. 2021-0058. It revises job descriptions for Director, Office of Ombudsperson; Deputy Director, Office of Charter Schools; Director, Payroll; Director, Budget and Finance; and Coordinator, Pre-K Systems and Operations. It also creates a job description for Accounts Payable Technician III. The agenda text gives no salaries or dollar amounts.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $9,900 for Be a Mentor's vendor management system and background checks
output.summary: The Board is ratifying a software license with Be a Mentor, Inc. of Hayward, CA, which will host the district's Vendor Management System. The system handles background clearances and arrest notifications for up to 120 district vendors. The term is July 1, 2020 to June 30, 2021, which began before this vote.

output.headline: Partners with Oakland Public Education Fund at no cost to survey families and distribute computers
output.summary: The Board is ratifying a no-cost agreement with the Oakland Public Education Fund's Tech Exchange Project. The group will survey district families about their need for devices, help hand out computers and Wi-Fi hotspots, and compare its records with district records. The two sides will also share student data under a separate data privacy agreement. The term is August 3, 2020 to June 30, 2021.

output.headline: Amends the board's charter schools policy to match state law changes effective July 1, 2020
output.summary: The Board is adopting amendments to Board Policy BP 0420.4 (Philosophy - Charter Schools). The changes bring the policy in line with state law changes that took effect July 1, 2020. No dollar amount is involved.

output.headline: Amends Measure G1 middle school grant plan for Community School for Creative Change Charter School
schools: Community School for Creative Change Charter School
output.summary: The Board is adopting Resolution No. 1920-0261C, which carries a recommendation from the Measure G1 oversight commission (Teacher Retention and Middle School Improvement Act). It amends the 2020-21 charter middle school grant application and education spending plan for Community School for Creative Change Charter School. The award uses the school's approved 2020-21 funding allocation. The agenda text does not state a dollar amount.

output.headline: Approves minutes of the September 9, 2020 regular Board meeting
output.summary: The Board is ratifying the minutes of its Regular Meeting of September 9, 2020, which staff prepared shortly after the meeting. No dollar amount is involved.

output.headline: Gives Development Group more time on a federal E-Rate technology contract because of COVID-19
output.summary: The Board is approving Amendment No. 1 to the 2019-20 Category 2 E-Rate application and contract with Development Group, Inc. to provide technology equipment and services. E-Rate is a federal program that helps pay for school technology. The amendment only extends the contractor's time to perform because of COVID-19, and all other terms stay the same. No new dollar amount is stated.
